category_mapping: BUILTIN.DF(customer.category) 2026-09-05: 2 = Garage Experts (excluded), 3 = DIY, 4 = Contractor, 7 = CA Will Call (kept), 14 = Vendor (excluded)
definition: Population: customer.stage LIKE 'CUSTOMER%' AND firstorderdate IS NOT NULL, c.subsidiary = 2, category NOT IN (2,14), datecreated in 2025-01-01..2026-05-31 (cohort = creation month; 1,480 customers, all present in the transaction join). NET revenue = canonical join from net_revenue_monthly.sql (CustInvc/CashSale/CustCred/CustRfnd, t.subsidiary=2, mainline='F', taxline='F', item not null, itemtype not null, SUM(-foreignamount)). First order date = the customer's earliest NET-positive transaction date (NOT customer.firstorderdate: 688 of 1,480 customers have $0 NET dated firstorderdate because the invoice/cash sale posts 1-5 days after the order date; the literal definition would count those first invoices as reorders). first_order_net = NET of all lines dated that first date; bands <400, 400-2499, >=2500. reordered = any transaction with transaction-level NET > 0 dated strictly after the first order date; one_and_done = customers - reordered; reorder_rate_pct = reordered/customers*100. time_to_second_order: gap = first such later date minus first order date, over reorderers only; median and share of reorderers with gap <= 17/30/60/90/180 days. small_vs_mid_relative_gap_pct = (rate_under_400 - rate_400_2499) / rate_400_2499 * 100 (relative, not points). Pulled as a band x gap_days histogram, one creation month per SuiteQL call (17 calls, 598 histogram rows), aggregated in Python.
